judgments.yea_description: Voted for Senate Bill 3. It would create a state prescription drug affordability board. The board could review drugs whose costs burden patients or the health system and set upper limits on what insurers, Medicaid and other buyers in Michigan pay for them. Limits could not apply to drugs in short supply, and the board could not use cost measures that value the lives of older, sicker or disabled people less. The Senate passed it 20-15. The House has not voted on it, so it is not law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for Senate Bill 29. It would require the state health department's plan to reduce racial and ethnic health disparities to also address inequities. The department's website would have to link to peer-reviewed studies on biased or unjust care for pregnant patients, including obstetric racism and obstetric violence. The Senate passed it 22-14. The House has not voted on it, so it is not law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for Senate Bill 31. Starting in 2027, it would require hospitals to let a patient giving birth have a partner or spouse and a doula present throughout the stay, or a doula and another companion if there is no partner, with limited exceptions. Hospitals would also have to state their informed consent policy and accept transfer information from midwives. It would add pregnancy and breastfeeding to the sex discrimination hospitals may not practice. The Senate passed it 22-14. The House has not voted on it, so it is not law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for Senate Bill 33. It would let a person's advance directive say which life-sustaining treatment the person wants or refuses if pregnant. It would end the rule that a patient advocate may not refuse treatment for a pregnant patient when that decision would result in the patient's death. The Senate passed it 19-17. The House has not voted on it, so it is not law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for Senate Bill 37. It would require health insurers that cover gynecological and pregnancy care to cover that care whether it is given at an in-network facility or at home, by an in-network doctor, certified nurse midwife or midwife. The Senate passed it 27-9. The House has not voted on it, so it is not law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for Senate Bill 296. Starting June 1, 2027, it would bar hospitals from requiring registered nurses to work beyond their scheduled or on-call hours, except in a declared emergency, a mass casualty event, the first 4 weeks of a public health emergency, or certain ongoing procedures. A nurse could be held up to 2 more hours, or 4 at rural hospitals, when unexpected circumstances prevent relief, and would get 8 hours off after a 12-hour shift. The Senate passed it 21-16. The House has not voted on it, so it is not law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for Senate Bill 973. It would create a Michigan-run health insurance exchange, governed by a 12-member board, where people and small employers could compare and buy health plans through a website and phone line by January 1, 2028. The Senate passed it 20-16. The House has not voted on it, so it is not law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for Senate Bill 977. It would require the state insurance department to apply for a federal waiver to set up a reinsurance program, which helps pay the largest medical claims so individual market premiums can be lower, and to run the program if the waiver is approved. The Senate passed it 20-16. The House has not voted on it, so it is not law.
